proposed_topic_definitions.PROPOSED:DIACRITIC-SENSITIVE-CENSUS: A census whose term matching misses diacritic spellings of transliterated terms, so its negative results can be false negatives.

statement: The stage-1 raw scan behaves as diacritic-sensitive: raw_hits for this label correspond exactly to plain-ASCII occurrences of the terms, while diacritic forms are not matched. S0407, the object's own file, has no raw hit although it contains 'abhāva' 3 times, 'Hetvābhāsa' once and 'Nyāya-sūtra' 28 times (it is reached only through ledger anchors). S0231 contains 'abhāva'/'Abhāva' 11 times and plain 'abhava' once and has exactly one raw hit; S0237 has 3 plain occurrences and 3 raw hits. For labels whose terms are transliterated Sanskrit, a NEGATIVE-CENSUS or a GENUINELY-UNDEFINED-AFTER-CENSUS can therefore contain false negatives (a missingness mechanism correlated with transliteration style). Counts were made by whole-file reading of the reader output; the A.4 normalization itself was not inspected.
suggested_remedy: Add diacritic-folded (NFKD, combining marks removed) variants of each term to the stage-1 term set, or fold diacritics in A.4 normalization; re-run affected NEGATIVE-CENSUS dimensions.
